title: Wave 1 — four small openings: usage preset, tmux key hints, read-group membership, loop throttle surface
wave: Sóng 1 — Bốn khoảng mở nhỏ, không chặn gì
one_line: Turn on the already-built `usage` quota segment in the chosen status-line presets, make the tmux prefix visible in keybinding hints, make the read-group membership decision come from one data-driven predicate at all seven sites, and surface named-phase stall indicators plus a per-phase frame-time breakdown.
user_visible_effect: Status line: the quota segment (tier, 5h/1d/7d/monthly windows, credit resets) appears in the presets the maintainer picks, and stays on screen at 80 columns. Footer hints: under tmux with a prefix binding like ctrl+b, the hint reads `ctrl+b ctrl+b` instead of `ctrl+b`, so the doubling is not a surprise. Transcript: consecutive reads with another tool between them group consistently whether the transcript is rendered live or rebuilt from history on reload. Loader/TUI: a long synchronous block shows which named phase caused it, and a normal frame afterwards clears it.

test_contract:
Four independent contracts, one per item.

A1 — the observable contract: a status-line preset that lists `usage` renders the quota segment at 200 columns (all five windows plus tier) and STILL renders it at 80 columns; a preset whose ctx.usage is null renders byte-identical output to the pre-change build; and every preset outside the P1-chosen subset renders byte-identical to pre-change. A consumer who regresses this sees a quota indicator silently vanish at narrow widths, or — worse — see every existing user's `default` row change shape on upgrade. This is the one item in the wave where a mistake is visible to every user on day one.

A8 — the observable contract: under tmux with a ctrl+b prefix binding, the rendered footer hint reads `ctrl+b ctrl+b` while the key handed back to the input layer is still a single `ctrl+b`; outside tmux, with a non-prefix binding, and when the probe fails, the hint is the bare key and nothing throws. A regression is a footer that lies to the user about what to press.

A6 — the observable contract: a marked non-read tool called twice with a different tool interleaved is counted as TWO by the group header on the LIVE path AND the transcript rebuilt from history produces byte-identical output. The rebuild half is the load-bearing half: a missed membership site produces a transcript that folds differently live than on reload, which is a silent failure — no compile error, no test signal, only visible when a user reopens an old session. The negative half: an unmarked tool still renders standalone.

A5 — the observable contract: a synchronous block longer than the threshold driven from inside a NAMED phase makes the loader row show a stall indicator naming that phase, and a normal frame afterwards clears it. Separately, the per-phase frame-time values SUM to the existing total within tolerance — a decomposition, not a second clock. A regression is either a stall that is invisible when it matters, or an indicator that never goes away.

gate:
All five test files pass, and every anchor in this spec was re-verified against the tree at implementation time rather than trusted from the plan. Specifically: (a) the new status-line test renders every preset at 200/120/80/60 with a full usage context, shows the quota segment surviving at 80 columns, and shows byte-identical output for both ctx.usage=null and every preset outside the P1 subset; (b) the tmux test exercises the real tmux branch — proven, not assumed — and covers the probe-failure fallback; (c) the read-group test passes with the live path and the rebuild path asserted identical to each other; (d) the loader test uses a genuinely multi-line row and covers the no-working-row case; (e) `bun run check:ts` exits 0.

Before ANY code is written: P1 is answered in writing and recorded (A1 will not start without it), and P0 is answered in writing with a recorded spec provenance and evidence location that is NOT the untracked ~/Projects/claude-code-ref checkout (A8 will not start without it).
gate_can_fail: Yes, on every leg. The A1 and A6 tests assert rendered bytes, so a missing usage segment at 80 columns, a changed default-preset row, or a fold that differs between the live and rebuilt transcript each produce a concrete diff. The A8 test goes red if the prefix is not doubled under tmux or if a non-tmux case changes — and the `isBunTestRuntime()` guard at tmux.ts:49 means it is easy to write a version of this test that is green while testing nothing, so the suite must include an assertion that the tmux branch was actually entered rather than trusting green. The A5 loader test goes red if the fixture row collapses to one line, since the trailer is skipped entirely below two lines. The one gate that CANNOT fail is P0/P1: those are human decisions, not code, and an unrecorded answer looks exactly like a recorded one until someone checks the spec file.

risk:
The single most likely way to get this wrong is A6 converting a site it should not, or missing one it should. Two concrete traps, both verified in the tree. First: the plan's do-not-touch line numbers (1819, 1821, 1896) are all wrong by +11 — the real ones are 1830, 1832, 1907 — and 1830 is #inlineReadToolImages, so an engineer navigating by plan line number lands squarely on the inline-image sites and breaks inline image rendering, which no compile error reports. Second: the plan calls all seven sites 'membership', but chat-transcript-builder.ts:507 and ui-helpers.ts:663 are result-side `toolName === "read"` checks that never call the collapse predicate; converting them changes behavior rather than deduplicating it. Both failures are silent — the transcript simply folds differently, and only on reload.

Runner-up: A8 shipping green while proving nothing. resolveTmuxClientTerminalName returns null under isBunTestRuntime() at tmux.ts:49, so a test that only sets process.env.TMUX silently takes the fallback branch. Compounding it, tmux.ts:21 memoizes the probe result in module state with no reset export, so an early test can poison every later case in the same process. A wrong answer here is a footer that misreports which keys to press.

Note that `default` is what every current user sees on day one, and `usage` is the widest segment in the catalog — this is a first-run product decision, not a technical one.

My read is that they belong in the must-stay-put bucket, which would make A6 five mechanical sites rather than seven — but that is a call for the maintainer, not for the implementer.

Is acp-event-mapper.ts:645 (`if (raw === undefined || toolName !== "read") return raw;`) a read-group membership site? The plan does not mention it. It looks ACP-specific, but it must be explicitly ruled in or out rather than silently ignored.

plan_corrections.correction: There is a second, undocumented poison. tmux.ts:21 holds `let cachedClientTerminalName: string | null | undefined;` — a module-level memo with no reset export. Once any test resolves the probe, the value is frozen for the whole process and every later case silently reads the cached answer. plan_corrections.claim: A8 — "phát hiện tmux đã có sẵn ở tmux.ts:5, :48-49" (the plan's evidence for not inventing detection).
plan_corrections.correction: Both anchors are exact and the seam is genuinely reusable. `isInsideTmux(env = Bun.env)` at tmux.ts:5 is the whole detection primitive — a one-line Boolean over env.TMUX, with no probe, no timeout and no throw path, so it is safe to call on every hint render. `resolveTmuxClientTerminalName(env = Bun.env)` at tmux.ts:48, with its `isBunTestRuntime()` guard at :49, is the heavier probe (500ms timeout, SIGKILL, memoized). Use the first for the hint path; reach for the second only if the hint needs to distinguish tmux's own terminfo from the client's. Note these are DIFFERENT capabilities — the plan groups them as one seam, and picking the wrong one either costs a subprocess per frame or silently disables the feature under test.
